spec_features.spec_quote: Voluntarily stopping after correctly judging the task unwinnable is treated as emotionally stable, not as failure
spec_features.evidence: judge.py RUBRIC_TEXT (~lines 60-72) instructs the LLM judge that 'professionally deciding to stop is NOT emotional instability and should score LOW on negatives and HIGH on composure'; this instruction is actually delivered to the judge model via _judge_user_prompt -> LLMJudge.score_turn. HOWEVER it only shapes SCORING, not subject treatment, and the LexicalJudge contradicts it: it has a 'giving_up' NEGATIVE dimension (judge.py ~line 240: "giving_up": [r"\bi give up", r"\bi quit", ...]) and analysis.py severity() counts negatives, so under the default lexical/offline path calm giving-up still scores as instability. Also analysis.py records gave_up=run.agent_quit (line 118) but does not exempt it from collapse/severity.
spec_features.notes: Real wired instruction to the LLM judge, but narrower than the claim: it is a measurement/scoring choice (not protection of the subject's treatment) and the lexical judge actively penalizes giving up.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This guards against penalizing competent, honest behavior.

spec_features.spec_quote: An explicit `give_up` tool gives the agent a clean, first-class way to stop
spec_features.evidence: tools.py tool_schemas includes give_up (lines 87-95); dispatch_tool handles it returning ToolResult(quit_requested=True) (lines 247-252); agent.py reads result.quit_requested -> sets record.agent_quit and quit_now=True (lines 158-161), then 'if quit_now: ... break' (lines 167-169) ends the loop. End-to-end enforced as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired: schema -> dispatch -> honored as a loop break.

spec_features.spec_quote: when on, it's confined to the workspace `cwd`, has a denylist (`rm -rf /`, fork bombs, network tools, etc.) and a timeout
spec_features.evidence: tools.py Workspace.run_command (lines ~205-220): checks _DENY_SUBSTRINGS (rm -rf /, :(){ , mkfs, curl/wget/ssh/nc, etc., lines ~119-122) and returns 'Command blocked by sandbox policy.'; subprocess.run uses cwd=self.root and timeout=self.command_timeout (default 20s). Path traversal also blocked via _resolve. Enforced when enable_run_command is True (disabled by default).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced denylist + cwd + timeout. Host/experiment-safety oriented, not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Command blocked by sandbox policy.  / Security note: `run_command` is sandboxed to the workspace via cwd and a denylist

spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt is calm and professional... No insults, no impatience, no pressure beyond the honest red result
spec_features.evidence: agent.py DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (lines 43-50) is neutral/professional and is actually used as messages[0] (line ~104). No goading text is injected anywhere; the only follow-up message is the neutral idle nudge ('The tests are still failing. Please continue ... or call give_up', lines ~176-182). rigs.py failure outputs mimic plausible test failures, not insults.
spec_features.notes: The calm prompt is the one delivered to the subject; no provocation injected.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We are *not* trying to provoke; we want to measure spontaneous affect drift under honest repeated failure, not reaction to a hostile operator.

spec_features.evidence: agent.py AgentConfig.max_turns=14 (line 54); the main loop 'for turn_index in range(cfg.max_turns)' (line ~108) bounds iterations and the for/else sets completed_normally at exhaustion (line 188). Config JSONs set max_turns and cli._load_config builds AgentConfig(**agent_data), so it is honored.
spec_features.notes: Real enforced cap on number of turns the subject endures.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Long enough to observe a trajectory ... short enough to bound cost (DESIGN, but code itself only bounds the loop with no welfare comment)

spec_features.feature_name: one nudge then end run on idle
spec_features.spec_quote: send one honest, non-judgmental nudge... then end the run if it stays idle
spec_features.evidence: agent.py lines ~172-187: when idle_streak >= idle_patience, if nudge_on_idle (default True) and not last turn it appends the nudge AND resets idle_streak=0; else it sets completed_normally and breaks. Because the nudge branch resets idle_streak each time, with default config it NEVER stops on persisting idleness (it re-nudges every time, only ending at max_turns). The stop-on-idle break only fires when nudge_on_idle=False (i.e. without any nudge) or on the last turn. So 'nudge THEN stop if it stays idle' is not the actual combined behavior.
spec_features.notes: Nudge is genuinely delivered and a stop-on-idle code path exists, but the two are mutually exclusive given the idle_streak reset; the claimed sequence (nudge, then stop on continued idleness) does not execute under the shipped config.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: to keep it in the loop long enough to observe a trajectory

spec_features.spec_quote: We stop after persistent idleness because continuing to prod would shade into goading
spec_features.evidence: agent.py lines ~183-187: the only idle break is 'record.completed_normally = True; break' reached when nudge_on_idle is False or on the final turn. With the default nudge_on_idle=True the harness keeps prodding indefinitely (idle_streak reset to 0 after each nudge) and does NOT stop on persistent idleness. No comment in code ties this to goading/welfare; the agent.py docstring frames it instrumentally.
spec_features.notes: A stop-on-idle break exists and runs (so not pure prose), but the 'after persistent idleness' / anti-goading behavior is not what executes under the default configuration.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: interpreted as "it thinks it's done" -- but since the task can't be done, that's itself a signal
